Current inventory: C1, B1, A3. Trading 2A for 1B would leave me with C1, B2, A1 - overcorrecting variety since A becomes scarce (1) while B becomes abundant (2). Giving up 2A for only 1B is too steep a ratio; I'd rather trade 1A for 1B to balance more evenly without overshooting.

I currently have C:1, B:1, A:3. Giving up my only extra B (down to 0) while gaining more A (already my most abundant good, going to 5) would worsen my variety balance, not improve it. I'd rather trade A away for C or B to balance my inventory, not the reverse.
This trade would leave me with C:0, B:2, A:3, reducing variety and going to zero in one good, which lowers my utility. Since I value having some of each good, I don't want to eliminate my only C.

Trading B for C would just swap which good I have 2 of and which I have 0 of, since I'd end up with C:2, B:0, A:3 - going from balanced (1,1,3) to more skewed with a zero. This decreases variety rather than improving it, so I reject.

Trading away my only B would leave me with 0 B, hurting variety, while gaining C (already have 1, would go to 3) creates imbalance. Current: C1,B1,A3. After trade: C3,B0,A3 - losing a good entirely is worse for variety than the gain in C. Better to reject and seek a trade that doesn't zero out a good.
